caption_text: CPU useful-update rates for the shallow-water and energy-balance models. Blue bars show ESM.md and orange bars show the hand-tuned baseline. A useful update counts one interior cell once per complete step. Required boundary calculations and redundant tile work remain inside the timer, without being counted as extra useful updates. Each point equals the useful update count divided by the median of twelve recorded times. Thin lines span the minimum and maximum of the twelve individual rates and are not confidence intervals. Each timing pair uses the same processor, grid, complete step count and buffers for the two implementations. Every measured CPU core budget has its own categorical position. No missing budget is interpolated. Each grid has an independent linear rate axis that starts at zero, with the same rate unit throughout the figure. The CPU core budget is the configured solver budget. The active worker count can be smaller for a small grid and is retained separately when supplied. The SW 64² cells workload has measurements at budgets 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 72, 128, 144, 248. The SW 256² cells workload has measurements at budgets 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 72, 128, 144, 248. The SW 1,024² cells workload has measurements at budgets 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 72, 128, 144, 248. The EBM 128 bands workload has measurements at budgets 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 72, 128, 144, 248. The EBM 4,096 bands workload has measurements at budgets 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 72, 128, 144, 248. The EBM 65,536 bands workload has measurements at budgets 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 72, 128, 144, 248. For the 128-band EBM grid, budgets 144, 248 use exactly 128 actual workers per route under the frozen band-count cap. The axis shows the configured budget, not a claim that every budgeted worker belongs to that team. The source record retains all times, batch lengths, source revisions, placement, worker counts, input identities and acceptance evidence.
